sentences.text: Bravasaurus measured roughly 7 meters in length and weighed nearly 2.9 metric tons.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes vertebrae, ribs, limb bones, and pelvic fragments, while the paratype contains an isolated tooth and additional limb and pelvic bones.
This animal was a small-sized titanosaur, significantly smaller than Punatitan and other medium-sized sauropods like Trigonosaurus, Overosaurus, and Bonitasaura.
Researchers suggest a connection between Bravasaurus and the contemporary Punatitan regarding the egg concentration found at the site.
Bravasaurus is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
The genus name Bravasaurus comes from Laguna Brava National Park in Argentina.
The species name arreirosorum honors the arrieros, 19th-century cattle drivers who crossed the Andes.
Phylogenetic analysis places Bravasaurus as a derived Lithostrotian within the clade Aeolosaurini, a subclade of Rinconsauria.
Bravasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago in what is now South America.
Fossils were found in sandstone layers 34 meters above the base of the Ciénaga del Río Huaco Formation at the Quebrada de Santo Domingo site in La Rioja, Argentina.
If the two specimens were adults, Bravasaurus would have been around 7 meters long, similar in size to Neuquensaurus or Magyarosaurus.
The time range for Bravasaurus is estimated from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
